paper.title: Fairness versus reason in the ultimatum game

headline: Nowak-Page-Sigmund 2000 ultimatum game (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; anonymous (w=0) q̄=0.064, p̄=0.190 (rational collapse) vs full reputation (w=1.0) q̄=0.967, p̄=0.570 (fair); q̄ rises monotonically with w

verdicts.gate: P1 no-reputation collapse: w=0 steady q̄ < 0.15 AND p̄ < 0.20 (evolution toward the rational near-0 offer)
P2 reputation -> fairness: w=1.0 steady q̄ > 0.30 AND p̄ > 0.30 (offers rise toward a fair split)
P3 reputation is the cause: (q̄ at w>=0.8) - (q̄ at w=0) >= 0.20 AND q̄ non-decreasing across w in {0, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0}

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the reputation-driven transition from the rational near-0 offer to fairness, and would catch an artifact

citations: Nowak, M.A., Page, K.M. & Sigmund, K. (2000). Fairness versus reason in the ultimatum game. Science 289(5485):1773-1775. doi:10.1126/science.289.5485.1773.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the population-mean acceptance threshold q̄ and mean offer p̄ across the reputation grid
